title: Efficacy of Inspiratory Muscle Training for Hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
author: Yoshito Kadoya

YK is the guarantor. YK drafted the manuscript.

A recent systematic review focused on RCTs regarding the effectiveness of RMT in patients with hypertension,5 in which load RMT may have a better effect on BP than unload RMT. However, this review was very heterogeneous due to the inclusion of the different types of respiratory training protocols applied. In addition, no clear benefit of the intervention on 24-hour BP, which is more closely associated with the incidence of CVDs,6-7 could be established Furthermore, because they did not use the GRADE approach, the uncertainty of each evidence is still unclear.5 In this study, we focused on the efficacy of high-intensity IMT, and aimed to investigate the available literature and determine whether high-intensity IMT improves 24-hour BP in patients with above-normal BP.
I: IMT with load (any level of load)

steps.title: High blood pressure (BP) is largely...
steps.instruction: High blood pressure (BP) is largely attributable to the risk of developing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs),1 which is an important cause of death in this era. Controlling BP is one of the essential risk modifications of CVDs. Several studies suggested that respiratory muscle training (RMT) lowers BP.2 Inspiratory muscle training (IMT) is a physical training that uses the diaphragm and accessory respiratory muscles to repeatedly inhale against resistance. Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) showed that IMT, especially high-intensity IMT, can reduce BP.3-4

3.2 Inclusion criteria of the articles for the review

steps.title: We will include randomized controlled trials...
steps.instruction: We will include randomized controlled trials that assessed the effects of IMT on BP and reported before and after ambulatory BP (mean 24-hour, daytime, and nighttime systolic and diastolic BP) in IMT and control groups. We will not apply language or country restrictions. We will include all papers including published, unpublished articles, abstract of conference and letter.

steps.title: We will exclude crossover trials, cluster-randomized, quasi-randomized and non-randomized trials
steps.instruction: We will exclude crossover trials, cluster-randomized, quasi-randomized and non-randomized trials. We will not exclude studies based on the observation period or publication year.

steps.instruction: Studied that had mixed interventions (e.g. IMT combined with breathing exercises) will be excluded.

steps.title: Two independent reviewers (YK and NS)...
steps.instruction: Two independent reviewers (YK and NS) will screen titles and abstracts, followed by the assessment of the eligibility based on the full texts. We will contact original authors if relevant data is missing. Disagreements between the two reviewers will be resolved by discussion, and if this fails, a third reviewer will act as an arbiter (KM).

steps.title: Two reviewers (YK and NS) will...
steps.instruction: Two reviewers (YK and NS) will perform independent data extraction of the included studies using standardized data collection form. We will use a pre-checked form using 10 randomly selected studies.

steps.title: The form will include the information...
steps.instruction: The form will include the information on study design, study population, interventions (including the intensity, duration, and frequency of IMT), and outcomes (24 hours ambulatory systolic and diastolic BP). Any disagreements will be resolved by discussion, and if this fails, a third reviewer will act as an arbiter (KM).
3.6 Assessment of risk of bias in included studies

steps.title: Two reviewers (YK and NS) will...
steps.instruction: Two reviewers (YK and NS) will evaluate the risk of bias independently using the Risk of Bias 2.9 Disagreements between the two reviewers will be discussed, and if this fails, a third reviewer (KM) will be acting as an arbiter, if necessary.

steps.title: We will pool the relative risk...

steps.title: We will pool the mean differences...
steps.instruction: We will pool the mean differences and the 95% CIs for the following continuous variables: 24 hours ambulatory systolic and diastolic BP, the incidence rate of all adverse events, systolic and diastolic casual BP, and the percentage of completed training sessions per prescribed training sessions.

steps.title: All intervention groups that are relevant...
steps.instruction: All intervention groups that are relevant to this review will be included.

steps.instruction: We will ask not-presented data to the original authors.

steps.title: We will perform the intention-to-treat (ITT)...
steps.instruction: We will perform the intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for all dichotomous data as much as possible.

steps.title: For continuous data, we will not...
steps.instruction: For continuous data, we will not impute missing data based on the recommendation by Cochrane handbook.10 We will perform meta-analysis about the available data in the original study.

steps.title: When original studies only report standard...
steps.instruction: When original studies only report standard error or p-value, we will calculate the standard deviation based on the method by Altman.11 If we don't know these values when we contact the authors, standard deviation will be calculated by confidence interval and t-value based on the method by Cochrane handbook10, or validated method.12 Validity of these methods will be analyzed by sensitivity analysis.

steps.title: We will evaluate the statistical heterogeneity...
steps.instruction: We will evaluate the statistical heterogeneity by visual inspection of the forest plots and calculating the I2 statistic (I2 values of 0% to 40%: might not be important; 30%to 60%: may represent moderate heterogeneity; 50% to 90%: may represent substantial heterogeneity; 75% to 100%: considerable heterogeneity). When there is substantial heterogeneity (I2> 50%), we will assess the reason of the heterogeneity. Cochrane Chi2test (Q-test) will be performed for I2 statistic, and P value less than 0.10 will be defined as statistically significant.

steps.title: We will search the clinical trial registry system (ClinicalTrials
steps.instruction: We will search the clinical trial registry system (ClinicalTrials.gov and ICTRP) and will perform extensive literature search for unpublished trials. To assess outcome reporting bias, we will compare the outcomes defined in trial protocols with the outcomes reported in the publications. We will assess the potential publication bias by visual inspection of the funnel plot. We will conduct Egger test to assess the publication bias. We will not conduct the test when we find less than 10 trials or trials which have similar sample size. We will also assess the potential publication bias by visual inspection of the funnel plot.

steps.title: Meta-analysis will be performed using Review Manager software (RevMan 5
steps.instruction: Meta-analysis will be performed using Review Manager software (RevMan 5.4.2). We will use a random-effects model.

steps.title: To elucidate the influence of effect...
steps.instruction: To elucidate the influence of effect modifiers on results, we will evaluate the subgroup analyses of the primary outcomes on the following factors when sufficient data are available.
